description: Codified rule making medication status deterministic (decision 16). Medication status is deterministic only relative to this artifact; a claim of active or discontinued medication is verifiable only by replaying these mappings over raw FHIR medication resources. The rule interprets recorded documentation, not clinical reality. v2 (P-08 v4 scope, 2026-08-27): a completed MedicationDispense no longer establishes active status - the exact-span audit of the v3 candidates rejected every dispense-implies-active inference, so a dispense alone resolves indeterminate and an active-status claim needs a MedicationRequest or MedicationAdministration.
notes: A resource whose effective date falls outside its recency window yields 'indeterminate', never 'not_active': stale documentation does not establish discontinuation.
An unmapped or absent status yields 'indeterminate' so that missing evidence produces abstention rather than a violation (decision 20).
Precedence resolves conflicts: the highest-precedence resource with a determinate result wins.

v2: MedicationDispense 'completed' moved from active to indeterminate. A completed dispense documents that a drug was handed over, not that the patient is on it; the v3 audit excluded 12/22 candidates for exactly this inference. Steering now guides such claims toward evidence-matched phrasing ('dispensed on <date>').
